title: Hello Beautiful
description: Four sisters in Chicago and the damaged young man who marries one of them. Little Women reworked, and the estrangement at its centre lasts decades.

title: Dear Edward
description: A twelve-year-old is the only survivor of a plane crash that kills his family. Alternates the flight with the years after.

title: My Sister's Keeper
description: A girl conceived as a tissue match for her leukaemic sister sues her parents for control of her own body. Picoult's method: an ethical dilemma, every viewpoint.

title: Small Great Things
description: A Black labour nurse is ordered not to touch a white supremacist couple's baby, and the baby dies. Told by the nurse, the father and the defence lawyer.

title: What Alice Forgot
description: A woman comes round after a fall having lost ten years, and cannot understand why she is divorcing a husband she still adores.

title: Apples Never Fall
description: A retired tennis coach's wife disappears and all four adult children privately suspect their father. Comic and then not, as usual.

title: Our Missing Hearts
description: An America where children are removed from parents deemed unpatriotic, and a boy looking for his Chinese-American poet mother. Libraries do the resistance.

title: On Earth We're Briefly Gorgeous
description: A letter from a Vietnamese-American son to a mother who cannot read it. Poet's prose, on labour, opioids and first love in Hartford.

title: Beautiful World, Where Are You
description: Two friends in their late twenties email each other about beauty, collapse and their unsatisfactory relationships. The emails carry the argument.

title: Intermezzo
description: Two brothers, a chess player and a lawyer, in the months after their father's death. Rooney's longest and most formally varied novel.

title: Dept. of Speculation
description: A marriage coming apart, told in numbered fragments with facts about astronauts and Buddhist monks between them. Under two hundred pages.

title: Weather
description: A university librarian answering mail for a climate podcast slides into dread. Same fragmentary method, aimed at the end of the world.

title: Outline
description: A writer teaching in Athens listens while other people talk about themselves. She is almost entirely absent, which is the technique and the subject.

title: The Friend
description: A woman inherits her dead friend's Great Dane in a New York flat that does not allow dogs. On suicide, writing and the animal in the room.

title: Small Things Like These
description: A coal merchant in 1985 New Ross finds a girl locked in the convent coal shed and must decide whether to notice. A hundred and ten pages, and complete.

title: Foster
description: A girl is left with relatives for a summer and finds out what being looked after feels like. Almost nothing is stated and everything lands.

title: Young Mungo
description: A Protestant boy and a Catholic boy in 1990s Glasgow, and the fishing trip Mungo's mother sends him on with two strangers.

title: Girl, Woman, Other
description: Twelve mostly Black British women across a century, in prose that dispenses with full stops. Shared the Booker in 2019.

title: Queenie
description: A Jamaican-British woman comes apart after a break-up, in a London that keeps telling her she is imagining the racism. Funny and hard to read at once.

title: Luster
description: A young Black woman sleeping with a married man ends up living in his house with his wife and adopted Black daughter. Very sharp, very uncomfortable.

title: Detransition, Baby
description: A trans woman, her detransitioned ex, and his pregnant boss consider raising a child between the three of them. Comic, and pointed about who gets a family.

title: Crying in H Mart
description: A musician's mother dies of cancer and she cooks her way back toward being Korean. The supermarket aisles do most of the emotional work.

title: Educated
description: Raised by survivalists in Idaho with no birth certificate and no schooling, Westover teaches herself enough to reach Cambridge. On what leaving costs.

title: Becoming
description: From the South Side of Chicago to the White House, with the parts about being a working mother given as much room as the campaigns.

title: Born a Crime
description: Born to a Black mother and a white father when that was literally illegal in South Africa. Very funny, and his mother is the real subject.

title: Wild
description: Eleven hundred miles of the Pacific Crest Trail alone, with no experience, after her mother's death and her marriage's end.

title: H Is for Hawk
description: Macdonald trains a goshawk after her father's sudden death, alongside T. H. White's account of failing at the same thing.

title: The Glass Castle
description: A childhood of squatting, hunger and a charismatic alcoholic father who promised a house made of glass. Told without a word of self-pity.

title: Know My Name
description: The woman known in court papers as Emily Doe writes the Stanford assault case back into her own name. On what a trial does to a witness.

title: When Breath Becomes Air
description: A neurosurgeon diagnosed with terminal lung cancer at thirty-six writes about what makes a life worth living. Unfinished, and his wife closes it.

title: In the Dream House
description: An abusive relationship between two women, told in short chapters each borrowing a genre. Written partly because the archive of such stories barely exists.

title: Heavy
description: Addressed directly to his mother, on weight, gambling, Mississippi and the things Black families do not say to each other.

title: Hunger
description: A memoir of Gay's body, and of the assault at twelve that she ate her way out of reach after. Refuses the transformation the genre expects.

title: A Thousand Ships
description: The Trojan war told entirely by its women, from Hecuba to the Amazons to Penelope losing patience by letter.

title: The Silence of the Girls
description: Briseis, a queen taken as Achilles' prize, narrates the Iliad from inside the camp. Barker writes the slavery as slavery.

title: Ariadne
description: The princess who gave Theseus the thread, and the sister he did not abandon. On the women myth uses and discards.

title: The Wolf Den
description: Enslaved women in a Pompeii brothel five years before the eruption. Researched from the actual graffiti on the walls of the Lupanar.

title: Hild
description: The girlhood of the woman who became St Hilda of Whitby, as a king's seer in seventh-century Northumbria. Dense with the period's texture and politics.

title: Wolf Hall
description: Thomas Cromwell from a blacksmith's yard to the centre of Henry VIII's government. Present tense, third person, and it changed the historical novel.

title: Bring Up the Bodies
description: Nine months in which Cromwell dismantles Anne Boleyn. Tighter than Wolf Hall, and it won Mantel a second Booker.

title: The Essex Serpent
description: A widow hunting a fossil in the Blackwater estuary and a vicar who thinks the villagers' sea serpent is a moral panic. Faith against natural history, in 1893.

title: The Miniaturist
description: A young wife in 1686 Amsterdam is given a cabinet-sized replica of her house, and the miniatures start arriving before the events they depict.

title: The Binding
description: Bookbinders take unwanted memories and bind them into volumes that must never be read by their owners. An apprentice finds a book with his own name on it.

title: The Mercies
description: A storm drowns forty men off a Norwegian island in 1617, leaving the women to run everything, until a commissioner arrives to look for witchcraft.

title: The Doll Factory
description: A doll painter in 1850 London becomes a Pre-Raphaelite model and acquires an admirer who collects things.

title: The Seven or Eight Deaths of Stella Fortuna
description: A Calabrian woman's near-fatal accidents across a century, and the silence between two sisters after they reach Connecticut.

title: The Island of Sea Women
description: Two women in the all-female diving collectives of Jeju Island, through Japanese occupation, war and a massacre nobody was allowed to mention for decades.

title: The Mountains Sing
description: A grandmother and granddaughter across Vietnamese land reform, famine and the war, told from inside rather than from the American side.

title: The Covenant of Water
description: Three generations in Kerala, in a family where someone in each drowns. Seven hundred pages by a physician, and the medicine is exact.

title: Cutting for Stone
description: Twin brothers born to a nun in an Addis Ababa mission hospital, and the surgeon father who fled. Ethiopia's coup, then a New York emergency room.

title: Shantaram
description: An escaped Australian convict runs a free clinic in a Bombay slum and falls in with the mafia. Nine hundred pages, and its relationship to fact is contested.

title: The White Tiger
description: A driver writes to the Chinese premier explaining how he became an entrepreneur, which involved killing his employer. Won the Booker.

title: Human Acts
description: The 1980 Gwangju uprising and its long aftermath, told by seven voices including a corpse. Han won the Nobel in 2024.

title: Bunny
description: A scholarship student at an elite MFA is absorbed by four women who call each other Bunny and whose workshop produces something alive.

title: My Year of Rest and Relaxation
description: A beautiful, wealthy, deeply unpleasant narrator decides to sleep for a year on prescription drugs. Set in 2000, ending where you expect.

title: The Idiot
description: A Harvard freshman in 1995 conducts a relationship almost entirely by email with a Hungarian mathematician. Very funny about being nineteen and literal.

title: Trust
description: Four documents about the same 1920s financier and his wife, each correcting the last. Won the Pulitzer, and the fourth section rewrites everything.

title: Bewilderment
description: An astrobiologist raising a neurodivergent son alone enrols him in experimental neurofeedback recorded from his dead mother.

title: North Woods
description: Four hundred years of one house in the Massachusetts woods, through apple growers, a painter, a schizophrenic and several beetles.

title: The Heart's Invisible Furies
description: Seventy years of a gay Irishman's life in seven-year jumps, from a girl thrown out of her village in 1945. Very funny and completely brutal.

title: Milkman
description: An eighteen-year-old in an unnamed Troubles-era city is pursued by a paramilitary and destroyed by gossip. Nobody in it is named. Won the Booker.
